title: AP Chemistry: Polyatomic Ions
description: Formulas, charges, and systematic nomenclature for essential AP Chemistry polyatomic ions.

cards.question: C₂O₄²⁻
cards.explanation: Oxalate (C₂O₄²⁻) is the dianion derived from oxalic acid (H₂C₂O₄) by loss of two protons.

cards.question: NH₄⁺
cards.explanation: Ammonium (NH₄⁺) is the positively charged cation formed by protonation of ammonia (NH₃).

cards.question: NO₃⁻
cards.explanation: Nitrate (NO₃⁻) has trigonal planar geometry. All nitrate salts are highly soluble in water.

cards.question: NO₂⁻
cards.explanation: Nitrite (NO₂⁻) is the conjugate base of nitrous acid (HNO₂). It has a bent geometry due to the nitrogen lone pair.

cards.question: SO₄²⁻
cards.explanation: Sulfate (SO₄²⁻) has tetrahedral geometry with sulfur in the +6 oxidation state. Precipitates with Ba²⁺, Pb²⁺, and Ca²⁺.

cards.question: SO₃²⁻
cards.explanation: Sulfite (SO₃²⁻) has sulfur in the +4 oxidation state and a trigonal pyramidal geometry.

cards.question: HSO₄⁻
cards.explanation: Hydrogen sulfate (HSO₄⁻), also called bisulfate, is amphiprotic with a pKa of ~1.99.

cards.question: OH⁻
cards.explanation: Hydroxide (OH⁻) is the Arrhenius base anion whose concentration defines the pOH and pH of a solution.

cards.question: CN⁻
cards.explanation: Cyanide (CN⁻) has a carbon-nitrogen triple bond. It is isoelectronic with CO and a strong-field ligand.

cards.question: CO₃²⁻
cards.explanation: Carbonate (CO₃²⁻) has trigonal planar geometry and reacts with strong acids to release CO₂ gas.

cards.question: HCO₃⁻
cards.explanation: Hydrogen carbonate (HCO₃⁻) is the primary physiological pH buffer in human blood plasma.

cards.question: PO₄³⁻
cards.explanation: Phosphate (PO₄³⁻) has tetrahedral geometry and forms the backbone of DNA, RNA, and ATP.

cards.question: HPO₄²⁻
cards.explanation: Hydrogen phosphate (HPO₄²⁻) is the mono-protonated phosphate and an intracellular buffer.

cards.question: H₂PO₄⁻
cards.explanation: Dihydrogen phosphate (H₂PO₄⁻) is amphiprotic—it can donate or accept a proton.

cards.question: ClO₄⁻
cards.explanation: Perchlorate (ClO₄⁻) has Cl in the +7 state and is a very weak conjugate base of the strong acid HClO₄.

cards.question: ClO₃⁻
cards.explanation: Chlorate (ClO₃⁻) has a trigonal pyramidal shape with chlorine in the +5 oxidation state.

cards.question: ClO₂⁻
cards.explanation: Chlorite (ClO₂⁻) features chlorine in the +3 state with a bent molecular geometry.

cards.question: ClO⁻
cards.explanation: Hypochlorite (ClO⁻) has Cl in the +1 state and is the active oxidizer in household bleach (NaClO).

cards.question: MnO₄⁻
cards.explanation: Permanganate (MnO₄⁻) has Mn in the +7 state. Its deep purple color is a classic redox indicator in titrations.

cards.question: CrO₄²⁻
cards.explanation: Chromate (CrO₄²⁻) has Cr in the +6 state and is bright yellow in basic conditions.

cards.question: Cr₂O₇²⁻
cards.explanation: Dichromate (Cr₂O₇²⁻) is orange in acidic solutions and in equilibrium with chromate (CrO₄²⁻) via pH.

cards.question: C₂H₃O₂⁻
cards.explanation: Acetate (CH₃COO⁻) is the conjugate base of acetic acid. All metal acetate salts are soluble in water.

cards.question: SCN⁻
cards.explanation: Thiocyanate (SCN⁻) forms a blood-red complex with Fe³⁺, used as a qualitative test for iron(III).

cards.question: O₂²⁻
cards.explanation: Peroxide (O₂²⁻) has an O–O single bond with each oxygen in the −1 oxidation state.

cards.question: IO₃⁻
cards.explanation: Iodate (IO₃⁻) is the conjugate base of iodic acid with iodine in the +5 state.

cards.question: BrO₃⁻
cards.explanation: Bromate (BrO₃⁻) has bromine in the +5 state with a trigonal pyramidal structure.

cards.question: S₂O₃²⁻
cards.explanation: Thiosulfate (S₂O₃²⁻) replaces one oxygen of sulfate with S. It is the standard titrant in iodometry.

cards.question: OCN⁻
cards.explanation: Cyanate (OCN⁻) is a linear anion. Wöhler's synthesis of urea from ammonium cyanate in 1828 launched organic chemistry.

title: AP Chemistry: Strong Acids & Bases
description: The 7 strong acids and strong soluble metal hydroxide bases required for AP Chemistry.

cards.question: HCl
cards.explanation: HCl is a strong monoprotic binary acid that fully dissociates: HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻.

cards.question: HNO₃
cards.explanation: HNO₃ is a strong oxyacid and powerful oxidizing agent that fully ionizes to H⁺ + NO₃⁻.

cards.question: H₂SO₄
cards.explanation: H₂SO₄ is a strong diprotic acid; its first dissociation is 100% complete, while HSO₄⁻ is weak (Ka ≈ 1.2×10⁻²).

cards.question: HBr
cards.explanation: HBr is a strong binary haloacid due to the long, weak H–Br bond.

cards.question: HI
cards.explanation: HI is the strongest common binary haloacid because iodide holds the proton very loosely.

cards.question: HClO₄
cards.explanation: HClO₄ has four electronegative oxygens pulling density from the O–H bond, making it extremely strong.

cards.question: HClO₃
cards.explanation: HClO₃ is recognized on the AP Chemistry exam as one of the 7 strong acids.

cards.question: Ba(OH)₂
cards.explanation: Barium hydroxide is a strong, soluble Group 2 base that yields 2 mol OH⁻ per mole dissolved.

cards.question: 私
cards.explanation: watashi or atashi, or "I", feminine, kanji.

cards.question: 悩んでいることはない
cards.explanation: nayandeiru koto wa nai, "to be unworried", kanji.

cards.question: 花見
cards.explanation: hanami, "going to see cherry blossoms", kanji.

cards.question: 書き初め
cards.explanation: kakizome, "first calligraphy of the new year", kanji.

cards.question: 馬の折り紙
cards.explanation: umanoorigami, "wishes hung up on shinto shrines", kanji.

title: Japanese: Verbs
description: Essential Japanese verbs with English questions and Hiragana answers.

cards.question: to see (an object)
cards.explanation: miru = 'to see / to look at / to watch'.

cards.question: to wake up
cards.explanation: okiru = 'to wake up / to get up'.

cards.question: to be in; to go in
to look for/to search for
cards.explanation: sagasu = 'to look for / to search for'.

title: Latin: Common Nouns & Articles
description: 30 common Latin nouns with English translations (including 'a/an/the').

title: Latin: Common Verbs
description: 10 fundamental Latin verbs translated into their 1st person singular ('I ...') form.

cards.question: ambulo
cards.explanation: ambulo = 'I walk' or 'I am walking' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: curro
cards.explanation: curro = 'I run' or 'I am running' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: dormio
cards.explanation: dormio = 'I sleep' or 'I am sleeping' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: scribo
cards.explanation: scribo = 'I write' or 'I am writing' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: lego
cards.explanation: lego = 'I read' or 'I am reading' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: cano
cards.explanation: cano = 'I sing' or 'I am singing' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: video
cards.explanation: video = 'I see' or 'I am seeing' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: audio
cards.explanation: audio = 'I hear' or 'I am hearing' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: voco
cards.explanation: voco = 'I call' or 'I am calling' (1st person singular present).

cards.question: laboro
cards.explanation: laboro = 'I work' or 'I am working' (1st person singular present).

title: Latin: Simple Phrases
description: Short phrases built strictly using vocabulary from the Latin Nouns and Verbs decks with correct subject-verb conjugation.

cards.question: Puella ambulat.
cards.explanation: puella (singular) + ambulat (3rd person singular of ambulo) = 'The girl walks.'

cards.question: Puer currit.
cards.explanation: puer (singular) + currit (3rd person singular of curro) = 'The boy runs.'

cards.question: Canis dormit.
cards.explanation: canis (singular) + dormit (3rd person singular of dormio) = 'The dog sleeps.'

cards.question: Feles videt.
cards.explanation: feles (singular) + videt (3rd person singular of video) = 'The cat sees.'

cards.question: Magister scribit.
cards.explanation: magister (singular) + scribit (3rd person singular of scribo) = 'The teacher writes.'

cards.question: Discipulus legit.
cards.explanation: discipulus (singular) + legit (3rd person singular of lego) = 'The student reads.'

cards.question: Rex vocat.
cards.explanation: rex (singular) + vocat (3rd person singular of voco) = 'The king calls.'

cards.question: Regina canit.
cards.explanation: regina (singular) + canit (3rd person singular of cano) = 'The queen sings.'

cards.question: Equus laborat.
cards.explanation: equus (singular) + laborat (3rd person singular of laboro) = 'The horse works.'

cards.question: Avis audit.
cards.explanation: avis (singular) + audit (3rd person singular of audio) = 'The bird hears.'

cards.question: The man sleeps.
cards.explanation: vir (singular subject) + dormit (3rd person singular of dormio) = 'Vir dormit.'

cards.question: The woman walks.
cards.explanation: femina (singular subject) + ambulat (3rd person singular of ambulo) = 'Femina ambulat.'

cards.question: The wolf runs.
cards.explanation: lupus (singular subject) + currit (3rd person singular of curro) = 'Lupus currit.'

cards.question: The servant works.
cards.explanation: servus (singular subject) + laborat (3rd person singular of laboro) = 'Servus laborat.'

cards.question: The friend reads.
cards.explanation: amicus (singular subject) + legit (3rd person singular of lego) = 'Amicus legit.'

cards.question: Puella canit et puer audit.
cards.answer: The girl sings and the boy hears.
aliases: The girl is singing and the boy is hearing.
A girl sings and a boy hears.
cards.explanation: puella canit (the girl sings) + et (and) + puer audit (the boy hears).

cards.question: Magister scribit et discipulus legit.
cards.answer: The teacher writes and the student reads.
aliases: The teacher is writing and the student is reading.
A teacher writes and a student reads.
cards.explanation: magister scribit (the teacher writes) + et (and) + discipulus legit (the student reads).

cards.question: Rex vocat et regina videt.
cards.answer: The king calls and the queen sees.
aliases: The king is calling and the queen is seeing.
A king calls and a queen sees.
cards.explanation: rex vocat (the king calls) + et (and) + regina videt (the queen sees).

cards.question: The man walks and the dog runs.
cards.explanation: vir ambulat (the man walks) + et (and) + canis currit (the dog runs) = 'Vir ambulat et canis currit.'

cards.question: The friend works and the cat sleeps.
cards.explanation: amicus laborat (the friend works) + et (and) + feles dormit (the cat sleeps) = 'Amicus laborat et feles dormit.'
